clue.text: Proclaim and declaim in the chair

definitions.note: a chair is a professorship, so this is the office itself

parts.note: to profess is to declare openly or proclaim
to orate is to declaim, speaking pompously

explanation.surface: An academic speechifies grandly while presiding over a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the chair' suggests chairing a meeting; here 'the chair' is a university professorship.
explanation.definitionFit: A university chair is a professor's post, and the professorate is that office or rank.

clue.text: Carriage from Westminster heading north to a school

indicators.note: in a down clue, travelling north means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: Westminster stands for the Houses of Parliament, abbreviated HP
Eton College is the famous English public school near Windsor

explanation.surface: A coach leaves Parliament and travels north to take someone to a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' reverses HP (Houses of Parliament, which Westminster stands for) to PH. ETON is the famous English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: A phaeton is a light open four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Love some abstract works at Tate Modern?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O
some of something is a part of it

explanation.surface: Someone is fond of a few of the abstract pieces in a London gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: Tate Modern is London's gallery of modern art; the question mark flags that it only exemplifies where such works hang.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is an abstract style using optical illusions, the kind of work shown in a modern gallery.

clue.text: Particular group of people without work N making a sort of escape

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the group's word wraps round the work

parts.note: an element is a distinct group within a larger body, as in the criminal element
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Some section of society, jobless, is making a getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', not 'lacking', so the work is wrapped rather than removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An elopement is running away secretly to marry, a particular kind of escape.

clue.text: Endless muck to make one lose weight

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: slime is sticky muck

explanation.surface: Getting covered in filth as a way to shed pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To slim is to diet so as to become thinner and lighter.

clue.text: Associated with spinning rubbish — a politician

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A political spin doctor is dismissed as talking nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotatory describes turning motion, relating to rotation or spinning.

clue.text: Country bird trapped live

indicators.note: trapped means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A small bird is caught alive in some nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is a Himalayan region, now governed by China, often called a country.

clue.text: Footballer who acts like a baby?

definitions.meaning: a player who runs with the ball at their feet past opponents
a baby lets saliva run from its mouth, playfully a person who does so

explanation.definitionFit: A dribbler both runs the ball past defenders and drools like an infant.

clue.text: Plan to be at home having nurse

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
to tend is to nurse or look after

explanation.surface: Someone plans to stay home with a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend is to have in mind as a purpose, to plan.

clue.text: Biological expert is a follower of Democritus

parts.note: an is the form of the indefinite article before a vowel
Democritus, the Greek philosopher, taught that matter is made of atoms; his followers are atomists

explanation.surface: A scientist turns out to be a disciple of an ancient Greek thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: An anatomist studies bodily structure, a specialist within biology.

clue.text: Lord, there's nothing harvested, it seems!

indicators.note: it seems here means it sounds like, so a word is said aloud

parts.note: land that yields no crop is barren

explanation.surface: A nobleman laments that his estate produced no crop.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a peer of the lowest rank, addressed as Lord.

clue.text: After short time see animal move unsteadily

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
an otter is a river mammal

explanation.surface: Shortly after, a wobbling creature is spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to walk with a shaky, unsteady gait.

clue.text: Volunteers housed in farm building, as may be disclosed

indicators.note: housed in means put inside a building, the word for which follows

parts.note: a stable is a building for horses
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve of volunteer soldiers

explanation.surface: Part-time soldiers are billeted in a barn, as might be revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Statable means able to be stated, that is, capable of being disclosed.

clue.text: Sleep needed by little man — endless sleep after being here?

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
Les is a short form of the man's name Leslie

explanation.surface: A small man needs a nap, and the place may bring on everlasting rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'See Naples and die': having seen it, death (endless sleep) may follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'See Naples and die' says nothing after this Italian city could compare, so death follows a visit.

clue.text: Maniac finally found out went to pieces

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before

parts.note: rumbled is informal British for found out or detected

explanation.surface: A madman, at last discovered, collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumbled means broke into fragments, literally went to pieces.

clue.text: A comedian out in the country

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: A stand-up comic is performing somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of A COMEDIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedonia, now North Macedonia, is a Balkan country.

clue.text: Completely unfashionable, favouring conservative politics

parts.note: out means out of fashion
the right wing in politics is the conservative side

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly dated and politically conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means wholly or completely, as in won outright.

clue.text: Flowering plant brought in by radiant husband

indicators.note: brought in by means the letters are carried inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bright spouse turns up with flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dianthus is the genus of pinks and carnations, garden flowering plants.

clue.text: Shortage of land to support duke

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so the duke's letter goes on top

parts.note: earth is land or ground

explanation.surface: Not enough ground is available to prop up an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack of something.

clue.text: Rare shock when Conservative gets in

indicators.note: gets in means one piece enters the other

parts.note: a scare is a sudden fright or shock

explanation.surface: An election surprise when the Tory wins a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce means seldom found, rare.

clue.text: Serious article penned by Hemingway

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, as in a pen, with a play on writing

parts.note: Ernest Hemingway was the American novelist
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grave piece written by the American novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and serious in manner.

clue.text: Retaliating fighters spraying nerve gas

indicators.note: spraying scatters the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Soldiers taking revenge attack with chemical weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Avengers are those who take revenge, fighters retaliating for a wrong.

clue.text: I'll take English and do it differently, right?

definitions.text: I'll take English and do it differently, right?

indicators.note: differently means the letters of do it are arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone offers to rewrite a piece of English and asks if that is all right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges DO IT into DITO between E and R. The whole clue is what an editor might say, taking copy and reworking it.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor takes in written English and revises it, making it read differently.

clue.text: The competition he avoided draw

indicators.note: avoided means the letters are left out

parts.note: a race is a competition of speed
he is taken as written and removed

explanation.surface: The contest that he skipped ended level.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace is to draw by copying lines, or to sketch an outline.

clue.text: Endless luxury brings advantage

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: plush means luxurious; as a noun it is the rich fabric of luxury

explanation.surface: Unlimited luxury gives someone the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is a benefit or advantage, an asset.

clue.text: Child's vehicle is hit — front comes off

indicators.note: front comes off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to strike is to hit

explanation.surface: A child's bike is struck and its front wheel falls off.
explanation.definitionFit: A trike is a tricycle, a three-wheeled vehicle for children.

clue.text: Plant girl exposed to the wind

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl
out in a strong wind is in a gale

explanation.surface: A young woman stands out in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Galingale is a sedge with an aromatic root, a plant related to ginger in cooking use.

clue.text: Statement perhaps from Holy Writ

parts.note: the clue word statement is one possible new arrangement of the letters of testament

explanation.surface: A declaration quoted from Scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: rework TESTAMENT and one result is STATEMENT; 'perhaps' shows it is one of several.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament is the Christian part of the Bible, which is Holy Writ.
